goal: Stops untrusted RPC method names and wallet names from injecting fake newline-delimited log lines into debug.log.
Makes the logger escape embedded newlines like other control characters instead of passing them through untouched.
reviewability: Ready to review now, last push already addressed the latest reviewer feedback and got a fresh approval the same day.
agreement: Strong support with code review approval from ryanofsky and ACKs from achow101 and polespinasa (achow101, polespinasa, ryanofsky).
Design discussion converged on escaping all newlines globally rather than RPC-specific sanitization, author adopted the simpler suggested approach.
Wallet-name-restriction commits were dropped after ryanofsky suggested keeping scope to logging, no remaining objections.

result.summary: This PR makes the logger escape embedded newlines (as \x0a) the same way it escapes other control characters, closing a path where restricted RPC callers or createwallet/restorewallet callers could inject newlines that forged additional, fake-looking log lines. It also adds a SplitLines helper so intentional multi-line output (exception traces, wallet transaction commit logs, wallet DB load errors, message-box text) is emitted as separate, properly-prefixed log entries instead of relying on raw embedded newlines. Tests were added/updated for SplitLines, LogEscapeMessage, RPC whitelist rejection logging, and wallet name creation logging.
result.problem: An attacker or misbehaving caller who can supply a rejected RPC method name or a wallet name (e.g. via createwallet/restorewallet) can embed a newline plus a crafted string that reads like a legitimate log line, confusing operators or forensic analysis of debug.log. This affects anyone relying on the debug log for trust, including via similarly-shaped injection points in the Tor control and I2P daemon integrations noted in review.

open_concerns: ryanofsky suggested also using SplitLines in walletdb.cpp:781 for readability; author applied it to the other spot but left this one as 'less cleanly applicable,' open for further comment.
ryanofsky had a mild preference to drop the separator banner in PrintExceptionContinue for simplicity; author kept it, no strong objection stated.
resolved_concerns: maflcko/davidgumberg raised whether newlines should be wholesale rejected across the whole log framework; author and maflcko agreed to scope that as a separate follow-up PR.
ryanofsky objected that per-site SanitizeString-based RPC sanitization was fragile/misleading; author reworked the PR to use global newline escaping instead, which ryanofsky then approved.
Wallet-name restriction commits were dropped after polespinasa/ryanofsky suggested leaving that to a dedicated wallet PR (#35768); author complied.

result.card: This PR fixes a log-injection vector where restricted RPC callers or wallet-name inputs could embed a newline plus forged text to make fake entries appear in debug.log, by making the logger escape embedded newlines like other control characters and by splitting genuinely multi-line diagnostic output (exceptions, wallet transaction commits, wallet DB load errors) into separate properly-escaped log lines via a new SplitLines helper. The strongest evidence of importance is that reviewers independently found the same class of issue elsewhere (davidgumberg noted Tor control and I2P daemon output can also inject control sequences), and maflcko explicitly wants this merged before a broader log-framework hardening follow-up, giving it leverage over future work. After design back-and-forth (RPC-specific sanitization was rejected as fragile in favor of a global newline-escaping approach suggested by ryanofsky), the PR was reworked and received Code Review ACK from ryanofsky plus ACKs from achow101 and polespinasa; no unresolved objections remain. It touches utils (the core logging fix), rpc and wallet (as the vectors demonstrated and tested), with the wallet-name-restriction idea explicitly scoped out to a separate PR (#35768). The PR is currently Ready for review with no known pending invalidating changes.
